records.issue: The estimated notification target may change with burden estimates or programme planning and is not the resident population.
records.misinterpretation: A high percentage is target achievement, not TB incidence or case-detection sensitivity.
records.extraMinimum: Retain the target vintage, estimation method and public/private notification scope.
records.check: Reconcile notified cases by sector and ensure the target belongs to the same geography and year.
records.compare: Compare only when target method, target vintage, notification scope and reporting year are aligned.

records.issue: Unknown HIV status can reflect missing linkage or delayed recording rather than absence of testing.
records.misinterpretation: Known status is not equivalent to HIV testing completed during the reporting period.
records.extraMinimum: Retain status-known date, test/linkage source and notified-TB denominator rules.
records.check: Confirm numerator is not greater than notified TB patients and quantify unknown or missing status separately.
records.compare: Compare only with the same definition of known status, notification cohort and linkage window.

records.issue: Eligibility and included drug-susceptibility tests can vary by guideline version and diagnostic pathway.
records.misinterpretation: Coverage does not establish test quality, result availability or regimen appropriateness.
records.extraMinimum: Retain eligible patient definition, test type, specimen date and result status.
records.check: Separate tests ordered, performed and resulted; deduplicate repeat tests for the same episode.
records.compare: Compare only under the same UDST eligibility rules, test menu and episode definition.

records.issue: Recent cohorts are incomplete and outcomes can be updated or reclassified after the initial report.
records.misinterpretation: Treatment success is a mature cohort outcome, not a contemporaneous monthly performance rate.
records.extraMinimum: Retain cohort start period, outcome cut-off, transfer status and final outcome classification.
records.check: Exclude immature cohorts and reconcile success, death, failure, loss to follow-up, transfer and not-evaluated totals.
records.compare: Compare only mature cohorts with identical outcome definitions and follow-up cut-offs.

records.issue: Payment processing, bank validation and benefit-status updates may lag clinical registration.
records.misinterpretation: Paid at least once does not mean every eligible instalment was timely or complete.
records.extraMinimum: Retain eligibility date, payment attempt, successful credit date and unique beneficiary identifier.
records.check: Deduplicate beneficiaries and separate initiated, processed, failed and successfully credited payments.
records.compare: Compare only when benefit rules, eligibility cohort and payment-status cut-off are aligned.

records.issue: Resistance category and appropriate regimen depend on test results, guideline version and documented clinical decision.
records.misinterpretation: Treatment initiation alone does not establish timeliness, adherence or favourable outcome.
records.extraMinimum: Retain resistance classification, diagnostic date, regimen, initiation date and guideline version.
records.check: Validate regimen against recorded resistance category and flag negative or implausibly long diagnosis-to-initiation intervals.
records.compare: Compare only under compatible resistance definitions, regimen guidance and initiation windows.

records.issue: Gestational age and registration date may be missing, estimated or entered retrospectively.
records.misinterpretation: The indicator measures timing among registered pregnancies, not population-level early ANC coverage.
records.extraMinimum: Retain registration date, gestational age basis and unique pregnancy episode.
records.check: Ensure first-trimester registrations do not exceed all ANC registrations and inspect missing gestational age.
records.compare: Compare only with the same first-trimester cut-off, pregnancy deduplication and registration denominator.

records.issue: Reported institutional deliveries and estimated deliveries come from different data-generating processes.
records.misinterpretation: Values over 100% may reflect referral, migration or denominator mismatch rather than simple over-reporting.
records.extraMinimum: Retain public/private delivery scope, residence versus occurrence basis and estimated-delivery method.
records.check: Reconcile institutional plus home deliveries and investigate values over 100% before correction.
records.compare: Compare only when denominator estimation, referral attribution and public/private coverage are aligned.

records.issue: Referral case-mix and facility capability strongly influence the caesarean proportion.
records.misinterpretation: A higher or lower value alone cannot be labelled better care without clinical-need and referral context.
records.extraMinimum: Retain total institutional deliveries, caesareans, facility type and referral/case-mix context.
records.check: Confirm caesareans do not exceed institutional deliveries and avoid averaging facility percentages.
records.compare: Compare like facility levels and referral roles using recomputed pooled numerators and denominators.

records.issue: A woman may receive multiple checks or appear across home and facility reporting pathways.
records.misinterpretation: The numerator should represent women receiving timely PNC, not the number of PNC contacts.
records.extraMinimum: Retain unique delivery episode, check date/time, delivery place and reporting facility.
records.check: Deduplicate women across contacts and verify the 48-hour interval from delivery time.
records.compare: Compare only with the same woman-versus-contact counting rule and delivery denominator.

records.issue: The denominator includes only live births weighed, so selective non-weighing can bias the rate.
records.misinterpretation: A low reported rate may reflect poor weighing completeness rather than low low-birth-weight prevalence.
records.extraMinimum: Retain live births, live births weighed, birth weight, timing and device/rounding practice.
records.check: Report weighing completeness alongside the rate and ensure low-birth-weight births do not exceed births weighed.
records.compare: Compare only when weighing completeness and measurement practice are sufficiently similar.

records.issue: Deaths after discharge or outside facilities may be missed or assigned to a different geography than births.
records.misinterpretation: A facility-reported neonatal mortality rate is not automatically a population neonatal mortality estimate.
records.extraMinimum: Retain live-birth denominator, neonatal death age, place of death, residence/occurrence basis and linkage method.
records.check: Validate age at death under 28 completed days and reconcile early/late neonatal death components.
records.compare: Compare only with aligned death ascertainment, geographic attribution, period and per-1,000 scale.

records.issue: The antigen schedule in the historical definition and the estimated infant denominator are source-version sensitive.
records.misinterpretation: This historical HMIS manifestation is not automatically equivalent to current full-immunization definitions or survey coverage.
records.extraMinimum: Retain eligible age band, antigen/dose schedule, vaccinated children, denominator method and source version.
records.check: Verify each required dose is represented once and investigate coverage over 100% without truncation.
records.compare: Compare only with identical age band, antigen schedule, denominator method and reporting source.

records.issue: BCG and measles counts may represent different birth cohorts, periods or catchment populations.
records.misinterpretation: A negative dropout value is a data/cohort signal, not coverage above perfection.
records.extraMinimum: Retain antigen dates, cohort/period alignment, BCG count, measles count and catchment definition.
records.check: Compute from counts rather than reported percentages; flag negative values and denominators of zero.
records.compare: Compare only when cohort, dose, period and catchment definitions are aligned.

records.issue: Due-list completeness determines the denominator and may differ across campaign rounds or localities.
records.misinterpretation: Coverage among listed due children is not population vaccination coverage.
records.extraMinimum: Retain due-list freeze date, unique child, vaccine/dose due, round and vaccination date.
records.check: Deduplicate children and reconcile newly identified children separately from the frozen due list.
records.compare: Compare only across rounds with comparable due-list construction and eligibility rules.

records.issue: Cancelled, merged, rescheduled and newly added sessions can change the planned denominator.
records.misinterpretation: Sessions held does not establish session quality, attendance or antigen availability.
records.extraMinimum: Retain microplan version, session identifier, planned date, actual date and disposition.
records.check: Reconcile held, cancelled, rescheduled and not-held sessions to the frozen microplan.
records.compare: Compare only with the same plan-freeze and rescheduling rules.

records.issue: The composite depends on which vaccines were required and whether stock-out was observed for the full session.
records.misinterpretation: A session-level stock-out proportion is not the same as vaccine wastage or warehouse stock availability.
records.extraMinimum: Retain session, required antigen list, stock status by antigen and observation timing.
records.check: Validate the any-stock-out composite from antigen-level status and keep not-assessed separate from available.
records.compare: Compare only with identical required-antigen lists and observation protocols.

records.issue: AEFI reporting is influenced by surveillance sensitivity, awareness, classification and investigation completeness.
records.misinterpretation: More reported AEFI does not by itself indicate less safe vaccination.
records.extraMinimum: Retain event classification, vaccination date, onset, notification date, seriousness and investigation status.
records.check: Deduplicate events and separate minor, severe and serious categories using the applicable guideline.
records.compare: Compare counts only with doses administered and comparable surveillance/classification practices.

records.issue: Confirmed cases depend on testing access and surveillance intensity as well as malaria transmission.
records.misinterpretation: Annual parasite incidence is not prevalence and a lower value may reflect reduced testing.
records.extraMinimum: Retain confirmed cases, population under surveillance, year, diagnostic method and testing volume.
records.check: Use the same population-year and triangulate with annual blood examination rate and positivity.
records.compare: Compare only with compatible diagnostic policy, surveillance coverage and population denominators.

records.issue: The numerator may count examinations rather than unique people, including repeat tests.
records.misinterpretation: Higher examination rate is surveillance intensity, not necessarily higher disease burden.
records.extraMinimum: Retain examinations, unique persons if available, test modality, population and year.
records.check: Confirm count unit and reconcile microscopy/RDT inclusion without double counting.
records.compare: Compare only when test modalities, repeat-test rules and population coverage are aligned.

records.issue: Positivity changes with testing strategy, case selection, season and diagnostic modality.
records.misinterpretation: A falling positivity rate may reflect expanded testing rather than reduced transmission alone.
records.extraMinimum: Retain positive tests, tests examined, modality, eligibility, place and period.
records.check: Ensure positives do not exceed tests examined and stratify microscopy and RDT when methods differ.
records.compare: Compare only with similar testing strategy, modality mix and season/period.

records.issue: Small death counts, delayed outcomes and inconsistent cause attribution can make the rate unstable.
records.misinterpretation: Case fatality is severity among detected cases, not population mortality risk.
records.extraMinimum: Retain confirmed cases, attributed deaths, outcome cut-off, diagnostic criteria and death-review status.
records.check: Ensure deaths are a subset of the case cohort and display counts with the percentage.
records.compare: Compare only with aligned case definitions, outcome windows and ascertainment; flag small numbers.

records.issue: The denominator must be the population of the defined endemic/elimination assessment unit, not an unrelated administrative total.
records.misinterpretation: Per-10,000 incidence must not be read as a percentage or per-1,000 rate.
records.extraMinimum: Retain cases, endemic-area population, assessment-unit boundary, year and per-10,000 scale.
records.check: Validate scale and geography; investigate boundary changes before trend comparison.
records.compare: Compare only within stable assessment units or after documented boundary harmonization.

records.issue: Reported drug consumption may differ from direct observation, distribution or verified ingestion.
records.misinterpretation: Distributed tablets are not equivalent to eligible people who consumed treatment.
records.extraMinimum: Retain eligible population, exclusions, persons treated/consuming, verification method and round.
records.check: Reconcile eligible, excluded, offered, treated and not-treated populations for the same round.
records.compare: Compare only with identical eligibility, exclusion and consumption-verification rules.

records.issue: Repeat screening and incomplete population enumeration can distort both numerator and denominator.
records.misinterpretation: Screening coverage does not measure diagnosis, treatment or disease control.
records.extraMinimum: Retain unique person, age eligibility, screening date, disease package, denominator source and prior-screen rule.
records.check: Deduplicate repeat screens and reconcile screened persons to the eligible enumerated population.
records.compare: Compare only with aligned age, disease package, screening interval and denominator method.

records.issue: Referral completion may be missed when diagnostic work-up occurs outside the reporting system.
records.misinterpretation: A screen-positive result is not a confirmed diagnosis.
records.extraMinimum: Retain unique person, screening result/date, referral, diagnostic completion/date and diagnosis.
records.check: Link diagnostic completion to the originating screen-positive episode and flag impossible date order.
records.compare: Compare only with the same positivity threshold, work-up definition and completion window.

records.issue: Treatment initiation may be recorded multiple times or outside the diagnosis-reporting facility.
records.misinterpretation: Initiation does not establish continuity, adherence or control.
records.extraMinimum: Retain unique person, confirmed diagnosis, treatment-start date, regimen and reporting facility.
records.check: Ensure initiation follows diagnosis and count one initiation per disease episode/person under the source rule.
records.compare: Compare only with aligned diagnosis criteria, treatment definition and initiation window.

records.issue: Control depends on disease-specific thresholds, measurement technique, visit window and retention in care.
records.misinterpretation: Control among measured clients in care is not population disease control.
records.extraMinimum: Retain diagnosis, measurement value/date/method, control threshold, care status and eligible cohort.
records.check: Apply the documented disease-specific threshold and report missing measurements/clients lost to follow-up.
records.compare: Compare only with identical thresholds, measurement protocol, cohort and observation window.

records.issue: A documented encounter may not represent completion of the clinically required follow-up pathway.
records.misinterpretation: Follow-up completion is not equivalent to diagnostic completion, treatment initiation or control.
records.extraMinimum: Retain screen-positive episode, required follow-up window, encounter date/type and outcome.
records.check: Verify encounter falls within the defined window and deduplicate multiple encounters for one episode.
records.compare: Compare only with the same follow-up definition, window and episode linkage method.

records.issue: Stock-out depends on the medicine list, observation period, item-day definition and facility reporting completeness.
records.misinterpretation: A facility with any stock-out does not show which medicines or how many days services were affected.
records.extraMinimum: Retain eligible facilities, medicine list, daily/period stock status, item, duration and reporting completeness.
records.check: Derive the facility composite from item-level evidence and keep non-reporting distinct from no stock-out.
records.compare: Compare only with identical medicine baskets, stock-out duration rules and facility eligibility.
